To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

- DAMA/NaIs have collected data over seven cycles and have pointed out at 7 σ C.L. the presence of a signal with all the peculiarities of the Dark Matter signature; - the signal is not due to any known background or side reaction; - the DAMA/LIBRAs are in operation since 2003 with a sensitivity of 10−2 pb; - the DAMALIBRA data analysis is in progress.

DAMA/NaIs are the only experiment to have clearly detected a positive signal compatible with the presence of Dark Mater particles in the galactic Halo, that the signal is well understood, that it is not affected by any side reaction or systematics, that it is model independent, that it has been confirmed over several annual cycles, that it is still ongoing and that it is the most solid evidence for Dark Mater particles to date.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and the use of large mass NaI(Tl), in the framework of the DAMA program, in order to search for WIMPs in the galactic dark halo.

1) the development of highly radiopure scintillating NaI(Tl): the main goal is to reach a background level in the region of interest (2-6 keV) of the order of a few events/(ton×year) and to study the possibility of a 1 ton NaIdetector; 2) the development of a 250 kg highly radio pure NaIdetector: the main goal is the confirmation of the observed effect and the study of
the investigation of the Dark Matter particle nature by exploiting the annual modulation signature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DAMA/LIBRa is still running and that the results of the first generation DAMA/NaL experiment have not been disproved yet.

the DAMA/NaIs have provided the first model independent evidence of Dark Matter particles in the galactic Halo, with an energy range from about 1.7 to about 70 keV, and that the model dependent corollary quests are in agreement.
the observed effect is still compatible with a Dark Matter particle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the low background DAMA experiments have provided a solid and unique evidence for the existence of Dark Matter particles, and that they are the only experiments in the world to have done so.
we have been able to demonstrate that the annual modulation signature is indeed there.

the low background DAMA experiments have been able to provide the first and still the strongest evidence for a Dark Matter particle candidate, and have also pointed out at a possible candidate for the Dark Matter particle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a large mass highly radiopure scintillating NaI(Tl), with a good energy threshold and resolution and with a very low background level, represents a powerful tool to investigate the presence of a Dark Matter particle in our galactic halo.

the DAMA/LIBRE experiment is able to provide an effective tool to investigate the presence of WIMP Dark Matter in the Universe, and that the annual modulation signature can represent a unique signature for Dark Matter.

the annual modulation signature is a very robust and powerful tool to investigate Dark Matter particles, which is able to effectively explore the whole parameter space of the model independent approach.
